**3.3** **_BF_** **Effect on** **_�C_** <sup>*****</sup>

Figure 8 displays the relationship between the BF and ηC <sup>*</sup>

according to the pintle orifice combination in each annular ring. Table 6 lists the filtering conditions and filtered
data average values. Because the effect of BF should be
evaluated under a similar TMR condition, the TMR range
was added as a filtering condition. In Fig. 8 and Table 6,
the BF and ηC <sup>*</sup> exhibited a weak proportional relationship
in each annular ring. In the case of P02A03 in Fig. 8c,
the efficiency was exceptionally low because the combustion pressure was not sufficiently increased compared to
the excessive propellant mass flow supply. Although the _BF_
increased by 14% from 51% when P01 was replaced with
P03, ηC <sup>*</sup> only increased within 0.74% at most in the A03
case. However, Ryu et al. revealed that ηC <sup>*</sup> increased by
3.85% from 92.63%, increasing in the BF of 15% from 70%
and a neglectable OFR increase of 0.05 [17]. Therefore, the
weak effect of the BF herein is probably due to two possible
reasons. First, the difference in mass flow rate allocation for
the rows is a factor. Ryu et al. allotted 30% of the area for the
second row but 17.5% in the present study. Therefore, the
smaller mass flow allocation for the second row may have
reduced the BF effect. Another possible reason for the relatively low BF effect on C <sup>∗</sup> in this study is the low BF values.
The BF change interval in this study was between 51 and
65%, whereas, in Ryu’s study, it was about 20% higher, with
70–85%. Therefore, the change in the direct collision mixing
efficiency of the propellants due to the increase in BF may
have been lower than in Ryu’s study. However, high BF can
cause thermal damage to the pintle injector [20]; additional
efforts are needed to optimize the BF under the condition that
thermal damage to the injector does not occur.

**Fig. 9** ηC <sup>_*_</sup> sensitivity to the TMR and BF

Figure 9 displays the ηC <sup>*</sup> sensitivities for the two
variables. In Fig. 9a, the ηC <sup>*</sup> sensitivity to the _TMR_ is
approximately 5, regardless of the BF changes. However,
as displayed in Fig. 9b, the sensitivity to the BF is 0.7 at A01
and approximately 2.65 for others. ηC <sup>*</sup> is less sensitive to the
BF than it is to the TMR. Furthermore, The BF can be less
sensitive in the strong momentum of the annular flow. The
cause of sensitivity to BF changed by TMR can be inferred
by referring to Cheng [15] and Ryu [17] together. Figure 10a,
b show the cases of A02 and A03 in Fig. 9b corresponding
to low fuel momentum. When the fuel momentum is low,
the deformation of the pintle jet from the first row orifices
is relatively minor. Then the flow width of the fuel vented
along the surface of the pintle post between the first row orifices can be broad. Under this condition, the increase of the
width of the second row orifices (a, b in Fig. 10) properly
contributes to enhancing the efficiency ensuing the effective
collision area ( _δ_ ) increase. Conversely, Fig. 10c, d, where the
fuel momentum is high, describe the A01 case in Fig. 9b. As
the fuel momentum grows, the deformation of the pintle jet
in the first row orifices increases and the width of the fuel
flow vented between the first row orifices becomes narrow.
With this situation, an increase in the width of the second
row orifices (c, d in Fig. 10) does not fully increase _δ_ .
